findings.issue: The 'settings omitted -> disabled' check (SPEC-01, A-1) cannot fail if the `settings === undefined` part of the disabled condition is removed. The helper passes `onSettingsChange={settings && noop}`, so the loading render has BOTH settings and onSettingsChange undefined, and `disabled={onSettingsChange === undefined}` alone still renders disabled. App always passes onSettingsChange, so in the real app the only thing keeping the checkbox disabled before the launch read settles is the untested `settings === undefined` clause. Same for the `settings &&` guard in onChange (renderToString cannot fire events, and no e2e can observe the pre-load window). Mutating SettingsScreen.tsx:41 to `disabled={onSettingsChange === undefined}` and :43 to `onSettingsChange?.({ ...(settings ?? DEFAULT_SETTINGS), ... })` passes every test, which is exactly the defaults-overwrite A-1 is meant to prevent.
findings.evidence: tests/ui/opponent-styles.acceptance.test.tsx:69-76 `onSettingsChange={settings && noop}` then `render(undefined)` at :90; src/ui/settings/SettingsScreen.tsx:41 `disabled={settings === undefined || onSettingsChange === undefined}`; src/ui/App.tsx:383-387 always passes `onSettingsChange={changeSettings}`.
findings.fix: In the SPEC-01 test, render the loading case the way App does: `<SettingsScreen onHome={noop} version="1.2.0" settings={undefined} onSettingsChange={noop} />` and assert the input is `disabled="" checked=""` (keep or add the both-undefined case separately). This is a locked test, so route the edit through the orchestrator.

summary: Implementation matches the spec. writeSettings validates with parseSettings before opening a transaction, uses strict durability and the shared memoised DB promise, so back-to-back writes are created in call order (SPEC-07 tests last-wins, extra-field stripping, and that an invalid write leaves the record unchanged). App reads the settings once at mount with a cancel flag, falls back to DEFAULT_SETTINGS and logs on rejection (the invalid-record e2e shows the next change repairs the record), updates state before saving, and logs save failures. Only the bot Seat's style span and its ' · ' are conditional. The user seat's aria-hidden separator and ReviewPanel are untouched, and SPEC-03 checks that the user seat markup is identical on and off. The locked e2e/settings.spec.ts keeps every original check (size, tag, Enter/Space, axe, version, origins). The name extraction only adds a label fallback, the expected list is re-pinned, and the tab-order comparison is the exact rotation `[...expected.slice(1), expected[0]]` approved in Block 1. Mutations such as labels hidden regardless of the setting (SPEC-04/SPEC-02), a skipped write (SPEC-05 poll, SPEC-07) or the user separator hidden (SPEC-03) would be caught. One gap: the disabled-until-loaded guard is not isolated by the SPEC-01 test (MAJOR). NIT, not filed: `.settings-toggle` adds `margin-top: 14px`, which the spec's CSS list does not name.
